item.title: Hi! can someone review my scp?: Forum Criticism Team - Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
ruffle5,

As per the Required Reading, all authors seeking conceptual critique must use the following template:

 **Seeking Greenlights:** Yes or No **Page Type:** SCP Article, Tale, GoI Format, Joke SCP, Site Dossier, Other (specify) **Genre (Optional):** Horror, Drama/Emotional, Comedy, Action, History, Other (specify) **Page Layout (Optional):** **Elevator Pitch:** **Central Narrative:** **Hook/Attention-Grabber:** **Additional Notes:**

Please edit your post to fit the specified format. Do NOT make a new thread. Instead, use the "edit" function, found below the post under "Options". In addition, please note that the last four sections of the template should not exceed 400 words. Do not link a sandbox draft unless a reviewer specifically asks.

Once you've made the changes, please refer to this thread to contact reviewers: http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/forum/t-13282692/how-to-get-more-reviews

item.title: Crimes Against Nature: Crimes Against Nature
item.content:encoded: My family is inherently Christian and they usually encouraged me to learn about all things holy. This concept is inspired by the ten biblical commandments and I intend to make it related to SCP-341 if I am allowed to.I don't think this concept has been done before, however I am probably wrong due to the massive amount of SCP's that have been created on this site. I am open to all criticism, and will improve on this concept as much as I can or need to.

item.title: Impossibly possible (greenlight wanted): Re: Impossibly possible (greenlight wanted)
item.content:encoded: I mean it sounds kind of intriguing? What conditions are we talking about here? I don't really know how the Foundation would be able to contain or even be aware of a probability range. To an average person it would just look like incredible luck or bad luck. I don't know what to say about the rest because the only thing you've really given ppl rn is that it's a probability range, (which now that I think about as an actual anomaly, sounds dull) and then you immediately start talking about Moon landing, which you give us 0 context about. Give us more man.

item.title: Twinportation: Re: Twinportation (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded: Like the other person in the thread said, this is just another "thing that does a thing". The concept itself is also just uninteresting, some beds that teleport you when you sleep? That's it? Are you not gonna expand upon where these people go? Why beds? And how would the Foundation even use it for teleportation? Can multiple people be on the same bed and still be transported? You never specified if it can be used to travel to your desired location, which if that is the case then you should add this stuff in the elevator pitch. You do know people aren't just up to sleep on the fly right? Assuming you have to actually sleep and be tired for this thing to work then this would be generally another usefully-useless anomaly. You also have to consider the fact that almost every article on Series VII is practically required to have a narrative to actually make it unique and the fact that you don't have one for this, which is an already lacking and pale idea is a little alarming.

item.title: It Will Not Leave: Re: It Will Not Leave
item.content:encoded:
Whoa, that was amazing. Thank you so much for such an extensive feedback. I will answer it without any order:

+ Some notes incoming
- Go
  • I agree with the Foundation attitude to the problem not being 'saving money'. I think the obvious approach would instead be that it would be risky to keep the guy in the MTF squad, as it might keep endangering other squad mates due to his unpredictability. As the situation escalates and Samuel is emotionally stopped from performing any activity, that would be another reason to separate him from the group. (edited in the OP)
  • I did not know about MTF Omega-0. I have not read thoroughly about it yet, but my understanding is that it uploads 'memories' to the SCP intranet? I might believe that if Samuel is troubled in his mind, syncing his mind/soul/spirit to the Foundation intranet might actually threaten the stability of Omega-0. It could even act as a cybervirus for the performance of the Omega-0 squad.
  • I understand that telling this story either as a Tale or SCP entails radically different structures. I can state two arguments why I think I would prefer to write this as an SCP file.
    • First, as a newbie writer I am not that confident yet on my strength in fully fleshing-out feelings of this kind in a Tale, without sounding exaggerated or hyperbolic. I am absolutely into subtlety, which ties with my second argument.
    • As you mentioned, one of the reasons why I did not write Adam's apparition to be real (aside from the mental health topic) is to play with the reader's expectations. Despite the clinical approach by the Foundation, the reader would nonetheless think that something is off. If we are telling the reader every time that Samuel is watching someone, she would be more prone to think that Samuel's right while the Foundation is missing something. As story progresses, amnestics result powerless and Samuel becomes physically constrained due to his mental strings, and so the reader would confirm her expectations.
    • One of the consequences of the SCP format is that the reader would actually never know if Adam's apparition was actually real or not. But I find that attractive, though. In this case, I think it would better work that the Foundation considers anomalous not 'Adam's apparition', but Samuel's mental problem, due to the resistance to amnestics.
    • Samuel's image becoming a memetic effect is something I am not quite sure, honestly. It may appear out of the blue, but it is another plot twist that I guess one does not see coming. If at all, one might expect Adam to appear to another MTF officer, not Samuel. But it might change the meaning of the whole writing by emphasizing the idea of Samuel's sorrow. Also, it rises the stakes for the Foundation, as it implies that what happened to Samuel might 'jump' to MTF officers and affect them, risking prospective MTF operations. The Foundation might establish as containment procedure that MTFs are to be monitored in case somebody shows any of the mentioned effects, isolate the guy to confirm it, and keep it alive for the time being.
  • The idea I explained as 'Central Narrative' was intended to stand as background: it would be told as you mention via medical/psychological reports, video logs from the missions, etc. Specifically, I had in mind to include one file acting as a HRM initial report at the moment of entry of Samuel; and another file being an interview with Adam and Samuel's mentor in police academy detailing their closeness. This second one could be included into the HRM initial report as well.
  • On Samuel's suicide, I understand it is a sensitive topic and difficult to pull off. The final twist requires him to die to make sense. A final addendum stating that Samuel appeared dead in his cell, then tying up with him appearing to another MTF officer seems too simple and anticlimactic. A suicide note seems also unconvincing and unoriginal, not to mention that he was reportedly unable to perform any action by that time.

That was a long response, I think I did not miss anything. Again, thank you so much for your help!

item.title: Impossibly possible (greenlight wanted): Impossibly possible (greenlight wanted)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional):

Page Layout (Optional): containment procedure (none) and then description, followed by multiple attempts at using the number.

Elevator Pitch: a specific probability range, when the conditions are reached becomes certain. For example, if you flipped a penny “the number” amount of times, you would reach your desired result. The “certain result” is decided by the intention of the system.

Central Narrative: A foundation researcher discovering the number through the first moon landing and several tests. The foundation then attempts to utilize it in multiple ways to contain SCPs.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: the SCP is an effect, not an object
Additional Notes: thanks for input in advance

item.title: A Balkan fairy tail: A Balkan fairy tail
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article
Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional, History

Page Layout (Optional): The article is made out of several camera and audio footages.

Elevator Pitch: The story is set in the Bosnian war. A girl with powers of a fairy is found in Bosnia. The Balkan MTF force captures her. Agent Kosta, an ethnic Croat born in Canada is sent to recover her but the Balkan base is atacked by the Chaos insurgency. The battle ends with Kosta and one insurgent as the only survivors. Kosta grabs the girl and they go through the war torn Bosnia, trying to reach the Croatian coast while runing from the still alive insurgent.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: As they drive through Bosnia, Kosta starts to bond with the kid. The child doesn't speak but communicates with Kosta by creating pictures on the various surfaces with her fairy dust. They meet various individuals from all three sides of the Bosnian conflict. In an abandoned coffy bar "Amsterdam", where all of the ethnicities laugh and drink together, while the girl, now going by the name Bojana Skadaric, plays with the other kids, he gets drunk and tells the sad fate of his wife, and how he lost her in a mission. His best friend Sam blamed him for her loss and they never saw each other again. The insurgent atacks the pub and destroys it. They reach an area controled by a Croatian warlord "Swedish" that commands a volunteer division while the local offical army unwillingly follows his orders. Swedish is in a blood feud with a local Serbian warlord. He finds out about the fairy abilities of the girl, as she intervened in an execution, but before he could capture her the Serbs start an offensive and the Serbian commander challenges Swedish to come out. Enraged, Swedish leads the volunteers to battle. The leader of the official army realises that his commander went completely insane, and orders the evacuation of the village. Kosta and Bojana go to the evacuation truck and is stoped by the voice of the chaos insurgent who calls Kosta by name, it is Sam. As he leaves to confront his former friend he tells the army leader to go far away with Bojana. He and Sam have only one bulet each and as they fire at each other a bomb drops between them, ending the footage.


Hook/Attention-Grabber: The story is about old conflicts that were never resolved coming to light. Bojana represents a generation not bound to those conflicts and has a future that she can choose freely, while Kosta, Sam and the people of Bosnia are chained to their fate.

item.title: Twinportation: Twinportation (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A set of twin beds that allow teleportation in between them. Sleeping in one bed will cause you to wake up in the other, regardless of distance between the two. The sleeper feels no change during the night, and cameras and surveillance of the bed during transport show the sleeper just vanishing.

Central Narrative: None.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A bed used by the foundation to transport quickly across long distances.

Additional Notes: Not an extremely deep entry, but I just think it sounds good.

item.title: Cannibalism Cantaloupes - Seeking Greenlights: Re: Cannibalism Cantaloupes - Seeking Greenlights
item.content:encoded:
They were discovered after contact with a village in Thailand (not sure about location yet) lost contact with the outside world and the villagers were found with melon plants coming out of their bodies.

Planting the seeds does produce a new plant, the document goes over the fact that seeds need to be destroyed in order to prevent new plants from growing.

If someone ate a subject of the effect doesn't transfer to them, a new melon plant simply grows out of them after a period of time.

item.title: Cannibalism Cantaloupes - Seeking Greenlights: Re: Cannibalism Cantaloupes - Seeking Greenlights
item.content:encoded:
Really cool concept — campy but pretty scary and interesting!

Questions:

  • Where do they come from? How were they discovered?
  • What about the seeds? Does planting them work?
  • After a person consumes a human subject of the effect, does the effect then transfer to them, as if they'd eaten a melon directly?
